corpus: Offline FLSA white-collar exemption (salary-basis) legal corpus
notes: The salary-level test for the executive/administrative/professional exemption -- federal (29 CFR §541.600) and California (Cal. Lab. Code §515). Tagged domain flsa_overtime because exemption determines overtime eligibility. Supports the misclassification demo (E006): an employee labeled exempt but paid below the applicable salary threshold fails the salary-basis test and is owed overtime. Verbatim anchors verified 2026-08-23 (Cornell LII / CA leginfo). Federal $684/wk = $35,568/yr is the 2019 level restored by DOL's May-2026 technical amendment; the CA threshold derives from 2x the state minimum wage.

chunks.title: Federal exemption salary level
chunks.text: To qualify for the executive, administrative, or professional (white-collar) overtime exemption, an employee must be compensated on a salary basis at a rate of not less than $684 per week (equivalent to $35,568 per year), in addition to meeting the duties test. An employee paid below this level cannot be exempt and is owed overtime.

chunks.title: California exemption salary threshold
chunks.text: In California, to qualify for a white-collar overtime exemption an employee must earn a monthly salary equivalent to no less than two times the state minimum wage for full-time employment. At the 2026 minimum wage of $16.90/hr this equals $70,304 per year; an employee paid below it cannot be exempt in California and is owed overtime.
chunks.verbatim_anchor: no less than two times the state minimum wage for full-time employment
